note: PUB-7 launch evidence: for each key or secret the public service depends on, where the replace-it-fast procedure is written down and where it was rehearsed. Names only, never values. A rehearsal is a test that changes the key in the local harness and proves people stay connected (or are signed out on purpose); it is never a production rotation. The readiness report checks that each procedure file exists and each rehearsal test name is really in its test file. A real-account rehearsal (really replacing a key on Chris's App) is an optional owner checklist row, not agent work.

secrets.name: Encryption key for saved GitHub credentials (TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, old key kept in TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS)

rehearsal.name: a key change does not sign people out

secrets.name: Routing key that signs every public connection (GITHUB_TENANT_ROUTING_KEY; the old key still checks until GITHUB_TENANT_ROUTING_KEY_PREVIOUS_UNTIL, at most 30 days ahead)

rehearsal.name: rehearsal: replacing the tenant routing key with an overlap window keeps people connected

secrets.name: The public GitHub App's private key (replaced on the setup page; GitHub checks the new key first)

rehearsal.name: rehearsal: replacing the App private key keeps installation tokens flowing, then only the new key is used

secrets.name: The public GitHub App's client secret (replaced on the setup page; GitHub checks the new secret first)

rehearsal.name: rehearsal: replacing the App client secret keeps GitHub sign-ins renewing, then only the new secret is used

secrets.name: The public GitHub App's webhook secret (made on the setup page; the old one is still believed for 24 hours)

rehearsal.name: rehearsal: replacing the App webhook secret loses no delivery, then only the new secret is believed
